## Both halves ship, and the second is the expensive one

Triage (`5353262802`) scoped this deliberately as **two** deliverables and named the risk of dropping one:

> Scope: `mkdir -p "$TARGET"` before the dump **plus** the misdiagnosis half — the failure branch that prints the Playwright remedy for a write failure is the more expensive half of this card and should not be dropped as a rider.

- **Half 1 (mechanical)** — `TARGET` is assigned at `:296` on `origin/main` and nothing creates it; `dump-public-manifest.mjs` calls `writeFileSync` directly. `mkdir -p "$TARGET"` before the dump.
- **Half 2 (the judgement)** — every failure branch here funnels to the same printed remedy, `pnpm exec playwright install chromium-headless-shell`. For a write failure that advice is **wrong**, and in a dispatch container it is **forbidden** (`PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1`, per `docs/releases-maintenance.md`). The browser had launched and the dump had succeeded; only the write failed. A reader following the printed advice chases the wrong layer — which is what cost the round this card was found in.

⛔ Shipping half 1 alone closes the ENOENT and leaves the misdiagnosis intact for the next failure mode that is not Playwright's. That is not a complete delivery of this card.

## Acceptance criterion

Reproduce the harm before and after: with `packages/console/dist/` absent, the current script dies `ENOENT … sdui.manifest.json` **after** paying for a vite dev server and a chromium launch, and prints the Playwright remedy. After the fix: the run completes, and — separately — a **non**-Playwright failure no longer prints the Playwright remedy. ⛔ A green run alone does not demonstrate half 2; the diagnosis path needs its own showing.

⚠️ Note why this matters more than the one-line fix suggests, from the card: `packages/console/dist/` is gitignored and exists only after a successful `scripts/build-console.sh`, so **a tree whose console build is broken cannot run the ADR-0082 D4 ratchet at all** — precisely when an independent read on the registry is most wanted. The ratchet does not even need the built dist: `gen-sdui-manifest.sh` drives a vite **dev** server over `.cache/objectui-*`.

⚠️ Adjacent, ⛔ **not in scope**: #10142 records that ADR-0082's addendum names three carriers of the `pnpm sdui:manifest` reminder and #10134 removed one of them. Different card, still `finding`, ⛔ do not fold it in — file anything you find, per the out-of-scope convention.

Gate families, taken from the tree at dispatch time (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs scripts/gen-sdui-manifest.sh`), not from memory:
- `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs` [lint.yml] · `node scripts/check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` [ci.yml]

⚠️ Line-of-sight list, **not a spec** — re-run the same script against your actual diff. `skip-changeset` expected (root `scripts/`), ⛔ but judge from your diff.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #10162. Reviewer of record: seat #6023, session `session_01DdCnBGcHeufjrq7drTD3wt`, 2026-08-20T12:3xZ (`date -u`).

Checked against GitHub and a named ref (`refs/pmcheck/10138`), ⛔ not against the PR body's self-description.

### Form

| item | reading |
|---|---|
| draft · base `main` · `Fixes #10138` first line | ✅ |
| changed files | 2 — `scripts/gen-sdui-manifest.sh` + `packages/spec/scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-write-target.test.ts` |
| `skip-changeset` | ✅ actually applied (verified on the PR, not inferred) |
| CI, latest per check-run name | 7 pending, **0 failing** |
| objectui's dumper untouched | ✅ absent from the diff — the surface fence held |

### ⚠️ Surface note, accepted with its consequences

The declared surface was `scripts/gen-sdui-manifest.sh`. The pin landed in `packages/spec/scripts/`, which is the **`domain:spec` seat's territory**. I checked the justification and it holds: `gen-sdui-manifest-cleanup.test.ts` and `gen-sdui-manifest-collision.test.ts` already live there driving this same script, so the placement follows the established convention rather than inventing one. And it does **not** touch `packages/spec/src/**`, so Clause ②'s path limb is not tripped.

Per this seat's standing rule — *范围内的文件 ≠ 范围内的卡* — the card stays mine and I take the consequences, which are real: the PR now pulls `Spec property liveness`, `Build Core` and the Dogfood gates instead of being a `scripts/**`-only change. Recorded, not charged against the run.

### Both halves shipped, and half 2 is demonstrated on its own

The ruling was that half 1 alone is not a complete delivery. It isn't one here:

- **Half 1** — `mkdir -p "$TARGET"` runs **with the other preconditions**, before the dev server and the browser. ⭐ That ordering *is* the fix: a `mkdir` placed next to the write would close the ENOENT while leaving the wasted vite+chromium prelude exactly where it was. Measured, not asserted — with `mkdir -p` unable to succeed, the harness footer reads `### exit=1 ### dev server spawned: 0 time(s)` against the successful run's `1`.
- **Half 2** — the dump's output is captured (`tee`, still streaming) and classified by a sourceable `sdui_dump_failure_advice`. ⭐ The fallback is **"unclassified"**, never "Playwright" — the report's own line is the right principle: *a classifier that guesses Playwright whenever it recognises nothing is the same defect wearing a conditional.*

⭐ `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` rather than `$?` after the `tee` pipeline. `$?` there is `tee`'s status and `tee` does not fail, so a plain `$?` would have read **every** dump failure as success — that is the #8727 trap, avoided in the diff that introduced the pipeline.

### The pin is designed against its own greenness — the part worth crediting

Five cases, all named, and both anti-vacuity moves are deliberate:

- a grep for `mkdir -p` would pass against one written *after* the dump, which fixes nothing about the cost — so the test measures the **order** (dev server spawned zero times vs once).
- a grep for the remedy string cannot distinguish a remedy printed *always* from one printed *on evidence* — so the real classifier is sourced out of the real script and fed real failure text in **three directions, including the Playwright case**. Without that third leg, "never blames Playwright" would be green for a script that prints no advice at all.

### Honest reporting, twice

- **The end-to-end run is impossible in this container and it says so** rather than papering over it (no vendored `.cache/objectui-*`, no Playwright browser, installing one forbidden here). The substitute is scoped precisely: the script is **copied**, which relocates `FRAMEWORK_ROOT` and therefore `TARGET`, so nothing could write into the real `packages/console/dist/`; port picking, detached spawn, liveness probe, failure branch and cleanup are all the real script.
- **The typecheck green was reverse-verified, with the mutation confirmed on disk** (`grep -c` = 1 and `git diff --numstat` = 2 added lines) rather than by an editor's exit code — then red in the predicted direction naming the file (`…write-target.test.ts(240,7): error TS2322`), then restored byte-identical and green again. ⭐ And it caught a pipeline trap while doing it: the lock wrapper printed `VERDICT command-exit 0` for that **red** run because the wrapped command ended in an `echo`, so the load-bearing readings are `tsc`'s own `Exit status 2` and the captured `TSC_EXIT=2`. That is the same `$?`-vs-real-status family as the fix itself, caught in the measuring instrument.
- **Two declared narrowings, neither hiding a red**: `check-dev-prereqs.mjs` exits 1 on any unbuilt worktree (a standing property, independent of this diff), and `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` needs the full closure and is left to CI — with the reason its per-file question is already answered by `check:scripts-typecheck`, which includes the file and carries zero ledger entries.

### Out-of-scope finding

**#10166** — verified filed, `finding` + `tooling` + `domain:devx`, unassigned, no `pm:queue`: `pnpm --filter <pkg> test -- <pattern>` swallows the positional filter and runs the whole suite (415 files / 358s, holding the shared verify lock for 6 minutes) **while reading as a targeted green**. Distinct from the zero-match family in #9089/#8727 — there the filter matched nothing; here it matched and the arguments were lost. ⛔ Not graded here — triage's channel.

#10142 correctly left open and unfolded.

### Disposition

**ACCEPT.** ⛔ Not flipping ready yet — 7 gate jobs still `in_progress`, and `in_progress` is an honest reading, not a pass. Ready + auto-merge on convergence, with enqueue verified against `refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/main/*`.

⚠️ One landing risk, named in advance: `Test Core` on this PR runs the very test file that flaked in the merge queue an hour ago (#10167 — `sdui_pick_free_port`'s TOCTOU race on port 5180), and this PR adds a **third** consumer of that port pool in the same package. If it dequeues on that signature, it is #10167's, not this PR's — and I will treat it that way rather than patching around it here.
